name: Svalbard
blurb: Polar bears, ringed seals, reindeer and seabird cliffs on Arctic tundra.

tip.title: Shrink the sea ice
tip.text: Select Sea ice and cut it by 50%. Watch the algae bloom, copepods, Arctic cod and ringed seals fall, and then the polar bears that hunt the seals.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Svalbard, Svalbard reindeer, Little auk). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Frozen sea surface that carries a bloom of algae, serves as a hunting platform for polar bears and a breeding platform for ringed seals.

nodes.name: Soil microbes & fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, carcasses and droppings slowly in the cold, returning nutrients to the thin soil.
Drifting microscopic algae that bloom in spring and summer in fjords and along the ice edge. They feed copepods and sink to feed the seabed.
A tiny creeping willow of Arctic tundra, a few centimetres tall. Reindeer and rock ptarmigan eat it.
Tiny, fat-rich crustaceans that graze the spring algae bloom and pass that energy to fish and seabirds.

nodes.name: Clams & seafloor bivalves
nodes.desc: Bottom-dwelling bivalves that filter food from the water and from sinking algae. They are a main food of walruses.

nodes.name: Svalbard reindeer
nodes.desc: A small, sedentary reindeer that grazes tundra plants all year. Nearly wiped out by hunting, it has recovered, but ice-sealed winter pastures can cause die-offs.
A small, abundant fish of cold water that eats copepods and is a key food for seals and seabirds.
A cold-water fish found in Svalbard lakes and rivers, with sea-going and lake-bound populations. It takes insects, crustaceans and small fish, and polar bears eat it.
Lives in and under sea ice, keeping breathing holes open and giving birth in snow lairs. It is the polar bear's main prey.
Digs clams from the seabed with its whiskers and snout. Hunted almost out of Svalbard by 1952, it has since recovered under protection.
A large gull that preys on seabird chicks and eggs, such as those of little auks, and takes seal pups and scraps.
Hunts and scavenges across tundra and shore, taking eggs, birds, reindeer and seal pups, including the leftovers of polar bear kills.
Svalbard's top predator, hunting ringed seals from the sea ice. It also takes reindeer, geese, eggs and walrus calves when seals are scarce.

story: Svalbard is an Arctic archipelago whose largest island, Spitsbergen, covers 37,673 km². Many seabirds breed here, and it is home to polar bears, reindeer and the Arctic fox. Polar bears have been reported eating little auk eggs.
matters: Research and tourism are important here. The University Centre in Svalbard and the Svalbard Global Seed Vault play critical roles in the local economy.
